transitions.description: Revision-2 artifacts and the Ed25519 name admitted at revision 2 (RFC 9864 alg-name bundle); legacy (EdDSA, 1) fixtures stay literally pinned
ML-DSA-44/65/87 admitted at revision 3; (EdDSA, 3) admitted; mixed-algorithm key sets legal (ml-dsa-admission ADR)
Seven timestamp members gained a 1..64 string-byte floor: long-fraction spellings the 0.2.x codec accepted now reject at the schema stage
max_artifact_set_bytes added to Limits (64 MiB default): previously verifiable oversized views now limit_exceeded under default limits
Improper-list inputs return typed errors instead of raising ArgumentError
PartyDescriptor effective_from gains the 1..64 string-byte floor its seven sibling timestamp members took in 0.3.0 — the last live timestamp asymmetry

A charter's parties must be distinct parties: a revision naming one descriptor for two roles rejects (revision_invalid), and a chain view whose revision parties resolve to one descriptor history, or that holds a history no revision names, rejects (chain_invalid)

Ed25519 public keys are fully decoded on admission: signatures using the identity and order-two negative-zero encodings return signature_invalid instead of ok; keys with no curve point are rejected, and signing preparation returns signing_key_invalid for all three encodings instead of ok
Limits structs with missing fields and profiles with improper algorithm lists return invalid_limits or invalid_profile instead of raising

Every retained and descriptive field type in caller-built revisions, descriptor facts, descriptor chains and chain facts is checked; malformed fields that 0.5.0 ignored and accepted now return invalid_type
Caller-built receipt revisions with a non-integer revision_number and chain facts with an invalid chain_topology or non-atom not_verified entries now return invalid_type instead of ok
Caller-built acceptance and termination descriptor chains with an invalid topology, and revisions with non-binary supersedes entries, now return invalid_type instead of ok
Malformed retained context fields, including improper lineage lists and non-binary envelope message or signature fields, return invalid_type instead of raising
Wrong context terms and malformed caller-built context field types use invalid_type consistently where receipt_invalid or descriptor_chain_invalid previously named an unusable context
Revision 8 admits descriptor key commitments, requires complete active-key openings, and admits unsigned current and next descriptor publication
Revision 8 admits distinct-role acceptance and termination quorums and unanimous declared party assignments.

A signed successor stays proposed until its immediate predecessor is accepted, including in legacy-signed-successor-of-unsigned-genesis. The child no longer governs, so a receipt bound to it returns receipt_claims_mismatch and signing its termination returns signing_refused.

Signing a legacy successor requires an accepted immediate predecessor and accepted supersession targets. See signing-legacy-successor-without-accepted-parent and signing-legacy-supersession-target-still-proposed. Signed sources still reject unsigned targets at set verification, even if the source stays proposed.
Descriptor histories are verified in ascending party ID order. The first invalid root in chain-many-histories-first-party-error returns descriptor_key_invalid instead of chain_invalid.

With three or more histories, set verification reaches history verification, revision decoding and admission. The chain-expanded-histories cases change chain_invalid to descriptor_chain_invalid, algorithm_outside_profile, revision_outside_profile, invalid_syntax, trailing_bytes, limit_exceeded, duplicate_member, non_canonical_bytes, invalid_type, unknown_member, missing_required, constraint_violation, cardinality_violation, nested_invalid, timestamp_invalid, revision_invalid, cross_field_invalid, extension_criticality_conflict, extension_duplicate, extension_namespace_invalid, extension_retired, extension_scope_invalid, or extension_unknown_critical.

With three or more histories and a valid revision-8 charter, invalid votes can reach envelope, binding and signature checks. The chain-expanded-histories vote cases return compact_invalid, protected_header_invalid, acceptance_claims_mismatch, termination_claims_mismatch, signature_invalid, invalid_type, missing_required, unknown_member, constraint_violation, timestamp_invalid, acceptance_invalid or termination_invalid instead of chain_invalid.
Elixir profiles recognize 8 as a range endpoint. The case chain-profile-endpoint-eight-admits-legacy-view verifies instead of returning invalid_profile, matching the TypeScript profile constructor.

Revision-8 acceptance and termination envelopes are admitted to claims checks. The quorum-acceptance-rejects-legacy-binding and quorum-termination-rejects-legacy-binding cases return their claims mismatch codes instead of protected_header_invalid. An ordinary signing operation with a replacement marker returns signing_refused instead of signing_input_invalid.

The revision-8 integer-token check covers acceptance, termination and assignment thresholds before canonical encoding or schema validation. The charter-revision quorum threshold cases return invalid_type instead of non_canonical_bytes, unknown_member or missing_required. A replacement object in place of the records array returns missing_required instead of unknown_member in charter-revision-replacement-container-missing-required.

With a legacy charter context, revision-8 acceptance and termination envelopes can reach signature length and claims validation. The quorum envelope cases return signature_invalid, invalid_type, missing_required, unknown_member, constraint_violation, timestamp_invalid, acceptance_invalid or termination_invalid instead of protected_header_invalid.

Standalone revision-8 vote verification reaches key resolution and signature verification. The quorum envelope cases for unresolved keys and invalid signatures return acceptance_invalid, termination_invalid or signature_invalid instead of unknown_member.

A receipt signed by the former holder in assignment-receipt-former-holder returns receipt_claims_mismatch instead of chain_invalid. Signing with only the bare revision-8 charter returns signing_refused instead of unknown_member.

The TypeScript verifier preserves the root signature error in chain-root-signature-before-revision: signature_invalid instead of descriptor_chain_invalid. A missing root key similarly returns descriptor_key_invalid in chain-root-key-error-before-revision.
The TypeScript verifier visits descendants before the next branch, returning descriptor_chain_invalid instead of revision_outside_profile in chain-history-descendant-before-next-branch.

The TypeScript verifier returns invalid_type instead of limit_exceeded for a non-text item before the item bound or in a list that exceeds the byte bound, including a hole in an oversized sparse array.

The TypeScript verifier checks the acceptance list before duplicate coordinates, so a later acceptance can return compact_invalid, protected_header_invalid, non_canonical_bytes, signature_invalid, invalid_type, missing_required, unknown_member, constraint_violation, timestamp_invalid, acceptance_invalid, acceptance_claims_mismatch, limit_exceeded, algorithm_outside_profile or revision_outside_profile instead of chain_invalid. See the duplicate-vote cases.

The TypeScript verifyChain entry point rejects a non-record set with invalid_type instead of chain_invalid. Set-aware builders return signing_input_invalid instead of invalid_type when malformed claims are paired with an invalid list inside a set.
Incomplete caller-built UTC datetimes and retained signing, key and digest inputs return typed failures through the Elixir public APIs.
